_meta.method: read by hand from the page-tagged text; monthly 'Estimated Savings' column sums to exactly 6,063, corroborating the p3 tile
_meta.why_it_matters: The only non-HSEnergy proposal in the set, and the only commercial one. It is the fixture that proves the extractor is not overfitted to one installer's template or to domestic-scale numbers.

_traps.export_kwh: GENUINELY ZERO. P5 states '0% Export to grid' and every month of the export column is 0. This is a correct 0, not a missing value. The old pipeline could not express this: applyExtracted() skipped any value not > 0, so the surveyor had to type the zero by hand.
_traps.os_roi: GENUINELY ABSENT. This proposal states no rate of return anywhere. Any value is a hallucination.
_traps.inverter_kw: 50 kW is stated on p4 ('50kW of Inverter Power', 1 x H350Plus). The p14 datasheet lists the whole H3 Plus range. 50/60/75/80/100/125, as decoys.
_traps.battery_kwh: 176.77 is the stated system total (11 x CQ16). Decoys: 159.09 kWh 'assumed usable capacity', 16.07 kWh per module on the p16 datasheet, and marketing copy 'Scalable from 64.28kWh to 241.05 kWh'.
_traps.annual_usage: 384,000 kWh. Commercial scale, roughly 186x the Varey Road figure. Any range check calibrated to domestic systems will misfire here.
_traps.system_cost: p7 reads '£236,931 Utility Bill Savings - £83,946 Net System Cost = £152,985 Estimated Net Savings'. Note p3 labels the price 'excluding VAT'.
_traps.os_payback: 'Payback 11 years' on p7. Note the implied payback from cost/savings is 13.8 years (83,946 / 6,063). A 25% divergence that is genuine, so a tolerance tighter than ~30% would false-positive on this document.
